# Song for a Daisy

This morning,  
as a school bell in the distance rings for a brief break,  
I lay myself down on a grassy patch,  
among daisies, swings, and seesaws,  
on daisies that spread wide like early spring cotton,  
white and unspoiled across the field,  
with here and there a splash of yellow sorrel  
that catches your eye in the sunlight —  

here where tiny feet and pushcart wheels crush the blossoms,  
and old folks stroll with their aging dogs along the paths,  
I caught the scent of damp earth and wet poplar leaves,  
drawing deep into my lungs,  
and in the umbrella of mushrooms  
poking through pine needles,  
my soul rejoiced  

like in a dream, I felt my limbs dissolve  
beneath the morning sun and the blue of the sky  
and let this old earth cradle me gently,  
and knew it was right —  
just like the daisies,  
I was here yesterday,  
but now I am gone.
